object_context: Type-I Navier–Stokes vorticity-geometry child. Determine whether the finite-I ancient class itself supplies any scale-critical vorticity-direction coherence sufficient for a published geometric depletion/regularity trigger, without importing a regularity property not inherited from the blow-up limit. Type-II remains out of scope.

root_binding.nonpromotion: Closing this atom would not close Type-II or the Clay root.

structural_coordinates: unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes; viscosity normalized to 1
parabolic scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), omega_lambda=lambda^2 omega(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
finite Albritton–Barker I is a local scale-invariant A+C+D+E cylinder bound and yields a nontrivial mild bounded ancient Type-I limit under source hypotheses
vorticity direction xi=omega/|omega| is meaningful only on nonzero-vorticity/high-vorticity regions
direction regularity differentiates a normalized first derivative of u and may require information beyond finite-I first-derivative energy control
Giga–Miura Type-I nonblowup uses uniform continuity of vorticity direction near large vorticity
Grujic arXiv:2607.08866v2 proposes a weaker local bmo_{1/|log r|} direction hypothesis but for an additional critical-point concentration scenario
local compactness and finite I do not automatically bind global/tail topology; prior NS-B1a3 gluing failure remains active
pressure is nonlocal but the present first discriminator is kinematic/geometric; any PDE inheritance claim must later restore pressure/evolution compatibility
functional calibrations are not Navier–Stokes counterexamples and cannot refute an equation-specific smoothing/coherence theorem

target_interface.input: nontrivial mild bounded ancient Navier–Stokes solution with finite I arising from a hypothetical Type-I singularity
target_interface.desired_output: an exact, scale-appropriate vorticity-direction coherence property matching a source-valid geometric regularity theorem
candidate_output_families: uniform continuity/coherence on high-vorticity regions (Giga–Miura calibration)
log-weighted bmo_{1/|log r|} coherence plus any extra concentration hypotheses required by the selected theorem
another geometric depletion quantity with explicitly proved inheritance
target_interface.audit_question: Can any such direction-coherence condition be obtained from the finite-I information class alone, or must it be a genuinely dynamics-specific new inheritance theorem?

solved_analogues.source: Giga–Miura, Comm. Math. Phys. 303 (2011), DOI 10.1007/s00220-011-1197-x; HUPSM 956
solved_analogues.fact: under a Type-I restriction, uniform continuity of vorticity direction where vorticity is large rules out blow-up
Type-I singularity is equivalent to a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with registered Type-I decay

near_solved_analogues.fact: for a critical-point concentration profile, local xi in L_infinity_t bmo_{1/|log r|} is used to obtain logarithmic vortex-stretching depletion and singularity evasion
finite-I local compactness does not itself supply a global critical rigidity topology

required_assumptions: direction field coherence in the exact theorem's norm/modulus
target_disanalogies: finite I controls local scale-invariant velocity/pressure quantities but no registered modulus of the normalized curl direction
zeros of vorticity make normalization singular
new 2026 bmo criterion is stated for a narrower critical-point concentration profile, not every finite-I ancient solution

method_transfers.source_context: a priori estimate from A+C+D+E only
required_assumptions: uniform consequence for every smooth divergence-free test field in the retained information class would be necessary for a purely functional proof

audit scaling/units of A,C,D,E for that family and avoid any claim that it solves Navier–Stokes
test both uniform-continuity modulus and log-weighted bmo mean-oscillation coordinates
